summary: Split shapes into parts and put the parts back together to make new shapes or designs.
Name shapes and describe what they are like, such as their sides and corners.
Use basic shapes to build, make or show real things, like a house from a square and a triangle.
Build with solid shapes like blocks and show how pieces fit together into new shapes.
Use position words to say where things are and how they fit together.
Use harder position words about place, direction and distance, like behind, toward or far.
Make a group of up to 5 things and say how many, using the last number counted.
See how many are in a group of up to 5 right away, without counting.
Count out loud to at least 10, and keep going on the way to 20.
Count 10 to 20 objects correctly, pointing to each one once.
Count a group with objects, fingers or drawings and give the total as the last number said.
Say the names of written numbers up to 10 when they see them.
Explain how an amount changes when some are added or taken away.
Spot, copy, continue and make up longer repeating patterns and sequences.
Notice and talk about patterns in nature and in things people make.
Measure and compare size, weight or how much things hold with objects or tools, and tell the result.
Describe measurements with comparing words like longer, heavier or holds more.
Collect simple information on their own, like counting who likes apples or bananas.
Organize information into simple charts, graphs or tables with an adult's help.
Use information they collected to answer a question, with an adult's help.
